title: Millimeter wave spectrum and search for vinyl isocyanate toward Sgr B2(N) with ALMA
question: To extend the laboratory rotational spectrum of vinyl isocyanate into the millimeter wave region and search for vinyl isocyanate and ethyl isocyanate toward Sgr B2(N) using the ALMA ReMoCA survey.

data.sensitivity: 0.35 to 1.1 mJy beam^-1 (rms) per spectral channel, median 0.8 mJy beam^-1

what.value: Microwave transitions and dipole moment components for trans and cis vinyl isocyanate

evidence.quote: its large dipole moment component along the $a$ principal inertial axis ($|\mu_{a}|=$ 2.047(6) D and $|\mu_{b}| =$ 0.824(9) D from (cite: Kirby1978)).
Our data set was finally combined with microwave transitions from (cite: Kirby1978)

what.value: Low-frequency microwave transitions and Stark dipole moments for cis vinyl isocyanate

evidence.quote: in agreement with the dipole moment components of $|\mu_{a}|=$ 2.14 (2) D and $|\mu_{b}| =$ 0.09 (2) D as determined by Stark spectroscopy (cite: Bouchy1979).
Our data set was combined with low-frequency transitions from (cite: Kirby1978) and (cite: Bouchy1977)

what.value: LTE parameters and column density of methyl isocyanate (CH3NCO) toward Sgr B2(N1S)

evidence.quote: we relied on the LTE parameters derived for methyl isocyanate, CH$_3$NCO, toward the same source by (cite: Belloche19) with the ReMoCA survey.

what.value: Spectroscopic entry 71508 (version 1) in CDMS and spectroscopic predictions for ethyl isocyanate

evidence.quote: We employed the spectroscopic entry 71508 (version 1) of the Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy (cite: Mueller05) to compute the LTE synthetic spectra of the torsional ground state
This CDMS entry is mainly based on the measurements reported in (cite: Kolesnikova18). For the first torsionally excited state, we used spectroscopic predictions from (cite: Kolesnikova18)

what.value: Energies of vibrational modes for ethyl isocyanate

evidence.quote: The upper limit given in Table [\[t:coldens\]](#t:coldens) accounts for the (substantial) vibrational correction that was estimated using the energies of the vibrational modes derived by (cite: Durig10) for ethyl isocyanate.

recipe.method: Coupled-cluster CCSD/cc-pVTZ harmonic and anharmonic force field calculations
key_parameters: convergence criteria set to 10^-8 atomic units

recipe.goal: Laboratory rotational spectrum assignment and Hamiltonian fitting
recipe.method: Loomis-Wood-type plot assignment and fitting to Watson's A-reduced Hamiltonian in I^r-representation
key_parameters: trans isomer: J_min/J_max = 4/80, K_a^min/K_a^max = 0/7, N = 464 lines
cis isomer: J_min/J_max = 1/61, K_a^min/K_a^max = 0/21, N = 608 lines
assumptions: For trans isomer, Phi_K = -471.8 Hz and phi_K = 21.58 Hz fixed to quantum-chemical values

recipe.goal: Compute rotational and vibrational partition functions and line catalogs
recipe.method: Numerical summation over ground state energy levels in SPCAT and harmonic/anharmonic vibrational mode summation
key_parameters: J up to 240, K_a up to 46 (trans); J up to 210, K_a up to 72 (cis)
assumptions: Energy difference between cis and trans isomers Delta E_ZPE = 301 cm^-1

recipe.goal: LTE synthetic spectrum modeling and column density upper limit determination toward Sgr B2(N1S)
recipe.method: Compute LTE synthetic spectra using Weeds and compare with ALMA ReMoCA observed spectra toward Sgr B2(N1S) to derive 3-sigma column density upper limits
key_parameters: theta_s = 2.0'', T_rot = 200 K, Delta V = 5.0 km s^-1, V_off = 0.0 km s^-1, V_sys = 62 km s^-1
F_vib = 4.00 for C2H3NCO; F_vib = 10.1 for C2H5NCO
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE); vinyl and ethyl isocyanate trace the same region with the same physical parameters as CH3NCO; LTE distribution between trans and cis conformers; single conformation for ethyl isocyanate

answer_key.quantity: Calculated energy difference Delta E_ZPE (cis - trans C2H3NCO)

evidence.quote: together with the energy difference between the *cis* and *trans* isomer of 3.6 kJ mol$^{-1}$ (301 cm$^{-1}$ or 433 K).

answer_key.quantity: Total rotational partition function Q_rot^(trans+cis) at 300 K
Column density upper limit of C2H3NCO (from trans-C2H3NCO, v=0) toward Sgr B2(N1S)
Column density upper limit of C2H3NCO (from cis-C2H3NCO, v=0) toward Sgr B2(N1S)
Column density upper limit of C2H5NCO toward Sgr B2(N1S)
Abundance ratio CH3NCO / C2H3NCO toward Sgr B2(N1S)

evidence.quote: We find that vinyl and ethyl isocyanate are at least 11 and 3 times less abundant than methyl isocyanate in this source, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Abundance ratio CH3NCO / C2H5NCO toward Sgr B2(N1S)

not_stated_but_needed: Exact CASA version and pipeline details used for the ReMoCA data reduction (inherited from Belloche et al. 2019 and Melosso et al. 2020)
Complete background synthetic spectrum model of all other identified molecules in Sgr B2(N1S) needed to assess line blending
Exact numerical value of distance to Sgr B2 adopted from Reid et al. (2019)
missing_for_reproduction: Extracted and continuum-subtracted 1D spectrum toward Sgr B2(N1S) from the ReMoCA survey
Full Weeds background model of all other identified species in Sgr B2(N1S) (grey/green curves in Figures 3-6)
Custom MATLAB Loomis-Wood assignment code from Vavra et al. (2020)
score_reason: The laboratory spectroscopy, quantum-chemical setup, partition functions, and JPL/CDMS line catalogs are completely published at CDS/CDMS, and the LTE parameters used in Weeds are explicitly tabulated in Table 3. However, reproducing the ALMA upper limits from scratch requires the specialized ReMoCA data reduction, continuum subtraction, and full multi-species background Weeds model from Belloche et al. (2019) and Melosso et al. (2020), which are not released with the paper.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA archival data (2016.1.00074.S) and the CDMS/CDS spectroscopic catalogs are publicly available, and the LTE parameters are fully specified in Table 3, allowing an agent to reproduce the synthetic spectra and verify the 3-sigma column density upper limits toward Sgr B2(N1S).
